lastReply:
People in India are switching to UPI because it makes paying someone as easy as sending a text, and it costs almost nothing. You open any payments app, scan a code or type a phone number, enter your PIN, and the money moves from your bank account in seconds. No cash to carry, no change to hunt for, no card machine needed.

For shopkeepers it is just as simple. A printed QR code on the counter is enough, so even a tea stall or a vegetable cart can take digital payments. That has pulled in millions of small sellers who never used cards.

It also works across banks and apps. You can pay from one bank to a person using a different app, at any time of day, including holidays. Add the cashback offers and the habit of seeing every payment in one history, and going back to cash starts to feel like a hassle.

Three main reasons:

Speed and ease: Pay in seconds with a QR scan or phone number, any hour of the day.
Low or zero cost: Most everyday payments carry no fee for the user, and shops need no special machine.
Works everywhere: One system links all banks and apps, from big stores to street vendors.
